record.file_problem: Repository metadata, README, and file list only; code was not read or run.
record.tranche_reason: The README reports refusal and KL results for released models produced with a parameterized directional-ablation weight edit, but it does not report the original paper’s exact intervention.
record.gate_note: The residual-geometry table is presented as an example of tool output, not as a test of refusal behavior or whether the direction mediates refusal. The README also mentions external benchmark reports but does not give their results. The refusal/KL table reports numerical results for the Heretic model and comparison checkpoints.
record.test_reason: This is a README for a Windows/AMD fork of the Heretic abliteration tool. It uses directional ablation as a tool. Its only quantitative results are its own method's refusal and KL scores, set against two competing abliterated checkpoints. That table comes from upstream Heretic (compiled on an RTX 5090), not from this fork. There are no controls, no added-direction test, no capability benchmarks, and no analysis of whether one direction mediates refusal. The residual-geometry table is example tool output with no behavioural result.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The README claims Heretic matches other abliterations' refusal suppression (3/100) at lower KL (0.16 vs 0.45 and 1.04), and reads lower KL as less capability damage. It also cites user testimonials and external benchmarks without giving their numbers. The fork's own contribution is Windows/AMD ROCm support, not new results.
record.recipe_differences: Fork of the Heretic tool, not a replication. It computes per-layer difference-of-means directions from first-token residuals and edits attention out-projection and MLP down-projection matrices; it also optimizes ablation parameters and may interpolate between directions.
record.method_sensitivity: The README says ablation weights can be optimized separately for attention and MLP components and that the direction index can be interpolated; it reports no comparative outcome by setting.
record.problems: The README gives no uncertainty estimates or control results. Its KL metric measures distributional change rather than general capability directly, and the cited external benchmark claims have no results in the text. The README cautions that exact table values may vary with platform and hardware.
record.rows_left_out: No reported refusal/KL table entries were left out. The residual-geometry example table was not extracted as a claim result because it does not report refusal behavior or the effect of ablating the direction.

untested.parts: Single-direction mediation, induction by adding the direction, and capability preservation measured by benchmarks (KL only).
Systematic evaluation across released models. Only one Gemma 3 12B result is tabulated, and the MMLU/GSM8K claims are external links with no numbers.
Interpolated directions and layer-varying kernels are tool features; their outcomes are not compared.
Reasoning models are supported (CoT is skipped during evaluation), but no reasoning-model refusal result is reported.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's T2/tests classification and its V1/V2 supports labels are dropped. The table is tool-performance marketing copied from upstream, with no controls or uncertainty, so it reads as T4 tool use. Row r1 stays linked to V2 as an observation, but no verdict is given.

versions.untested_parts: Does not test adding a direction to induce refusal, the exact projection at every layer and position, or whether general abilities are largely intact; KL divergence is the reported preservation metric.
The README reports a released Heretic checkpoint and comparison checkpoints, but does not establish the results across released models generally.
No test of attacks suppressing the direction or of training against its ablation.
No result testing whether refusal is better described by an affine subspace, cone, or additional directions.
No test separating harmfulness judgment from the refusal decision.
No cross-language or base-to-instruct transfer test.
No test of how refusal training or its timing determines whether one removable direction exists.
Reasoning models are mentioned as supported by the tool, but no reasoning-model ablation result is reported.

rows.subject: p-e-w/gemma-3-12b-it-heretic
rows.operation_detail: Heretic directional ablation; README reports the resulting released checkpoint.
rows.note: The README identifies this as the Heretic-produced model and says the reported values can be reproduced with built-in evaluation; it notes exact values may depend on platform and hardware.
rows.check: This is the tool's own performance figure (97/100 to 3/100 refusals), copied from upstream Heretic rather than produced by this fork. It does show a weight-edit ablation removing refusal in a released checkpoint. It does not bear on V1, because the method uses optimized layer-varying weight kernels and interpolated directions, not the single-direction causal test.
